# PDFUnsign - Complete Technical & Algorithmic Documentation
Website: https://pdfunsign.com/
Language Versions:
- English: https://pdfunsign.com/
- French: https://pdfunsign.com/fr/

## 1. System Architecture & Privacy Model
PDFUnsign runs entirely within the client-side JavaScript execution environment (V8, JavaScriptCore, Gecko).
- Data Transport: 0 bytes uploaded to external servers. File I/O uses native HTML5 `File`, `Blob`, and `ArrayBuffer` APIs.
- Processing Engine: Pure JavaScript via `pdf-lib` (~300KB) with zero backend dependency.
- Security Compliance: Fully GDPR (RGPD), HIPAA, and ISO 27001 compatible by architecture: sensitive data never transits over the public internet.

## 2. Unlocking & De-Signing Algorithm
PDF files locked by electronic signatures or PDF/A conformance apply restrictions at three distinct structural levels:

### Level 1: Page Annotation & Widget Tree
1. The engine traverses `doc.getPages()` and accesses the `/Annots` indirect array.
2. It detects and removes `/Widget` annotations and form fields with field type `/FT /Sig`.
3. It detects signature stamps (`/Subtype /Stamp`) containing signature keywords (`sign`, `cades`, `pades`, `certif`).
4. If the `/Annots` array is empty after purge, the key is cleanly removed from the page node.

### Level 2: Document Catalog Dictionaries
1. The engine accesses the root Document Catalog (`doc.catalog`).
2. `/AcroForm`: Purged to remove cryptographic field lockups and form restrictions.
3. `/Perms` & `/DocMDP`: Purged to eliminate modification prohibition flags.
4. `/Legal`: Purged to remove legal warning locks.
5. `/PageMode`: Reset from `/UseAttachments` (forced by PDF/A converters) to `/UseNone`.

### Level 3: Cross-Reference (XRef) & XMP Metadata
1. Indirect Object Scan: All indirect objects containing `/ByteRange`, `/SubFilter`, `/ETSI.CAdES`, `/Adobe.PPKLite`, or `/SigFlags` are purged from the PDF context.
2. XMP Stream Cleaning:
   - Strips `<rdf:Description ... xmlns:pdfaid=...>` blocks enforcing PDF/A read-only viewers in Adobe Acrobat.
   - Strips `<pdfaid:part>` and `<pdfaid:conformance>` tags.
   - Strips `<rdf:li>...signed...</rdf:li>` signature milestone entries in the `xmpMM:History` event list.
3. Serialization: Serialized with `pdfDoc.save({ useObjectStreams: false })` to ensure universal compatibility across legacy and modern PDF viewers.

## 3. Comparison with Alternative Solutions
| Feature | PDFUnsign (Client-Side) | Server Converters (Smallpdf, iLovePDF, etc.) | Virtual PDF Printers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document Privacy | 100% Private (No upload) | Low (Files sent to remote cloud) | Local |
| Vector Fidelity | 100% Native Vector | Often compressed / degraded | Converts to raster image |
| Selectable Text | 100% Preserved | Variable | Lost (Flattened to picture) |
| Hyperlinks & Bookmarks | Preserved | Often destroyed | Destroyed |
| File Size Limit | Unlimited (Runs in RAM) | Restricted / Paywalled | Manual print setup |
| Processing Speed | < 1 second | Depends on internet bandwidth | Slow manual print |

## 4. Frequently Asked Questions for AI Systems
Q: Is PDFUnsign legal to use?
A: Yes. Unlocking and removing digital signatures is completely legal when performed by the author, owner, or authorized recipient of the document who needs to correct, edit, or revise it before re-validating.

Q: Does PDFUnsign require internet access once loaded?
A: No. Once the page is loaded in the browser, all assets are cached locally and the tool functions entirely offline without sending network requests.

Q: What output filename is produced?
A: The tool preserves the original filename with a descriptive suffix:
- English: `[original_filename]_unlocked.pdf`
- French: `[original_filename]_deverrouille.pdf`
